PheWAS: variants across Analyses

Source: R/phewas.R
og_phewas.Rd

Returns the Associations of variants at p <= threshold, across every Analysis of the Store Releases (or the analyses you name). The query runs as Jobs on the API, and og_phewas() waits for them (see vignette("large-queries-and-jobs")).

Usage

og_phewas(
  src,
  variants,
  threshold = 1e-08,
  analyses = NULL,
  releases = NULL,
  limit = 1000,
  observed_only = FALSE,
  original_units = FALSE
)

Arguments

src

A Source, from og_api().

variants

rsIDs and ALIDs, such as c("rs1421085", "16:53767042:C:T"); an ALID must be in canonical form (see og_alid()).

threshold

The largest p-value to return; 1 returns every Association.

analyses

NULL (every Analysis of the Store Releases), or Analysis identifiers (see og_analyses()).

releases

Store Releases to use, as in og_analyses().

limit

The most Associations to return per ALID and group of up to 10 GWAS Stores, at most 10,000.

observed_only

Leave out Imputed Associations.

original_units

Give beta and se in the trait's original units, as in og_tophits().

Value

A data frame with the columns of og_associations() and og_provenance() attached.

Details

variants are rsIDs and ALIDs, mixed, as for og_associations(). An rsID is resolved to every ALID it names in the Store Releases (a multiallelic site names several), and opengwasr runs one PheWAS per ALID and combines them: you get every match, in the order the variants were given (an rsID's ALIDs in the order the API gave them). An rsID no Store Release holds gives a warning of class opengwasr_unresolved_variants, as for og_associations(). Every Job is in og_provenance().

With analyses = NULL (the default) every Analysis of the Store Releases is searched. The Analyses' metadata (beta's effect scale, n, ncase) is then looked up once, after the rows, for the Analyses that appear in them. What can be queried is the API's say: an Analysis in the result that the catalogue doesn't list yet is returned as the API sent it, with its metadata columns (effect_scale, n, sample_size_kind, ncase, ncontrol) NA, and no warning. original_units = TRUE can then only be refused (class opengwasr_original_units_unavailable) after the search, naming the Analyses in the result; name analyses and it is refused before any query runs.

The columns are those of og_associations(); rows are in the order the Jobs returned them (one per ALID, split by Store Release, each in the API's order). One Job takes at most 10 GWAS Stores and 100 Analyses, and a larger request is split and put back together as for og_associations().

limit applies to each ALID (not to all the variants together), and to each group of up to 10 GWAS Stores searched (the Store Releases are searched in groups of that size), so you can get more than limit rows in all. When it cuts any off you get a warning of class opengwasr_truncated, and og_provenance() has truncated = TRUE; total is the number of Associations that passed threshold. observed_only is always sent; opengwasr never relies on the API's default.

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
src <- og_api()
ph <- og_phewas(src, c("rs1421085", "16:53767042:C:T"), releases = "OGS-00011")
} # }
